name: Nïrwe
description:
When the Chthonic Subcommittee came into power, their first act was to throw up walls around their Citadel spanning the Great Chasm: the miles-long scar in the earth that gave the city its name. From this stronghold their cruel edicts were issued unopposed, and through their bureaucrats and mechanical Enforcers they regulated and oppressed magic throughout the land. A sad, desperate, dirty, chaotic city grew outside the walls, and with it a rising discontent.

Then came the Rising of the Bards, which through song spurred the people to throw down the gates and storm the Citadel. They found it hastily abandoned and the Subcommittee themselves fled deep into the Chasm. Then all chambers were thrown open, and many dear friends and enchanted things long-missed were found.

So began a merry and prosperous time: an age of free magic, of discovery and joy. Without the Subcommittee to choke the curiosity of the people, magic flowed from every fingertip in every corner of the land and for every purpose, great and humble.

But the unity of the rebels was brief. Factions quickly formed and each district of the city fell under the control of gang leaders who meted out their own justice. The city is now a tumult of alliances, power grabs, betrayals and assassination plots.

And all the while, though the abandoned Citadel appears empty and lifeless by day, by night it seems more and more to reawaken: strange lights are seen within the walls, shapes of wandering darkness roam the edges of the Chasm and the rusting bodies of the Enforcers are seen in one place one day are found elsewhere the next. Are all these things moved through some lingering magic of the Subcommittee, by some new evil taking root there, or by an old power creeping back in?
